description: American Express is a global financial company that specializes in payment cards for consumers and businesses, as well as travel services. The company’s green charge card has the distinction of being the world’s first charge card to be made out of plastic, replacing the paper cards that were in use prior to its 1959 introduction. Amex was founded as a freight forwarding company in 1850. American Express Travelers Cheques, introduced in 1891, made it possible for people to obtain cash in foreign countries, changing the nature of travel and the company’s profile. Over its history, American Express has owned a cable TV business as well as an investment bank. The company is currently organized into four business segments: U.S. consumer services, international card services, commercial services, and global merchant and networking services.

rankings.itemDescription: American Express has built its success as a globally integrated payments company through its connected workplace, the core of which consists of informal “coffee chats” that bolster employee collaboration, increase their visibility, and provide feedback to supervisors. This transparency and consistent employee input has proved vital in sustaining the Amex Flex hybrid and remote work system. Doubling its amount of free annual counseling sessions, Amex continues to expand its mental health services and also provides employee dependent care, eldercare, and support for parents of children with disabilities. Amex has maintained 100% pay equity for four years running and has exceeded its initial goal of providing, by 2024, capital and financial education to over 250,000 businesses run by underrepresented owners. Beyond sustaining connection and support within the company, Amex has pledged more than $30 million through 2024 as part of its Backing Small initiative to support economically vulnerable small business owners through grant programs, mentoring support, and technical assistance.

Beyond sustaining connection and support within the company, Amex has pledged more than $30 million through 2024 as part of its Backing Small initiative to support economically vulnerable small business owners through grant programs, mentoring support, and technical assistance.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription: For the third year in a row, American Express achieved 100% pay equity across gender globally, and across race in the U.S., unfortunately still a rarity for many firms. It also increased the number of employees who are eligible for company stock options; expanded mental health benefits; and began subsidizing virtual tutoring for workers’ children who need the extra help. Beyond those benefits, Amex continues to take the lead among its financial-firm peers in scheduling flexibility, allowing employees not required to be on-site full-time to “Work From Anywhere” up to 30 days a year. Some 80% of employees can work remotely day-to-day, while 99% of the workforce is eligible for hybrid work. Unlike other companies, Amex has proved its commitment to diversity and inclusion is more than just a talking point: The company is expanding its $1 billion investment in diverse suppliers and other such initiatives to $4 billion by the end of 2025.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription:
The 173-year-old global financial services company and payment card provider climbed eight spots on this year’s list.

  • Amex saw impressive revenue growth in 2022, at $55.6 billion, a 27% increase from the year prior.

  • However, the company’s $7.5 billion in profits in 2022 marked a 7% decline from the previous year.

  • In the first quarter of 2023, Amex reported record revenue of $14 billion, a 22% increase over the first quarter of 2022, but was bracing for increased credit card debt that would erode its profits.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription: American Express celebrates its 22nd year on the list, thanks in part to its flexible work policies, generous benefits, and a $1 billion diversity, equity, and inclusion initiative. Between late October 2020 and mid-2021, the company spent over $450 million on contracts with diverse suppliers, providing financial assistance and resources to minority-owned businesses, and improving pay equity internally, among other actions outlined in its first-ever DEI report. An outlier among the major financial firms, the company has also taken its workers’ calls for greater flexibility to heart. Employees haven’t been required to return to the office full-time; instead, more than 40% of staffers say they plan to stay remote, and the company is updating its offices and technology to make hybrid work easier for the rest, who will be required to come in two days a week at most.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: American Express benefited from a rebound in both leisure and business travel in 2021: The company notched 14% year-over-year revenue growth in 2021, and profit for the year nearly doubled, to $8.1 billion. The company also claimed significant success in signing up new millennial and Gen Z consumers for its premium credit cards. American Express broke with some of its financial-services competitors by launching and endorsing an official hybrid work model, dubbed Amex Flex, with hybrid workers reporting to the office roughly two days a week; the company reported in March 2022 that more than 40% of its workforce had chosen this option.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription: Last March, American Express made a commitment to not lay off a single employee owing to the pandemic in 2020—a pledge the company proudly says it upheld. AmEx provided workers impacted by COVID-19 with financial security at an uncertain time; it guaranteed full pay to those who couldn’t work because they or a family member were affected by the virus—without their having to use paid time off—as well as to those whose work sites were forced to close but who couldn’t do their jobs from home. Meanwhile, CEO Steve Squeri’s commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion is lauded by employees; after Squeri targeted 100% pay equity across the organization, AmEx says it achieved that goal last year for colleagues of all genders globally, and those of all races and ethnicities in the U.S.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: Business and leisure travel tanked as the pandemic forced companies and consumers to swap trips for Zoom meetings and staycations. That hit American Express hard, pulling the firm down 61 spots on the Global 500 this year as profits cratered nearly 54% in 2020. But things are improving for the credit card titan: Overall card member spending is on the rebound; AmEx CFO Jeffrey Campbell expects the firm’s embattled travel and entertainment spending segment to recover to roughly 70% of its 2019 levels by the fourth quarter; and the company is now aiming to achieve in 2022 the earnings it had originally expected last year.
